curation.why: method_invocation (8 occurrences) is a *call site*, not a declaration. The generator promoted it because it carries a `name` field and nests other declarations (an argument can contain a lambda), and it labelled it `method` — which is a container, so every `foo.bar()` would enter a breadcrumb trail as though it were a method declaration. Relabelled `call`, which is what the built-in Java profile does and what the label set reserves for exactly this. object_creation_expression is labelled `call` for the same reason: `new Invoice(items)` is a use site, and it matched on a `type` field. enum_body_declarations is the `{ }` wrapper holding an enum's members after the constants — the role C#'s declaration_list and Python's block play — and anchoring on it adds a level that names nothing; the enum_declaration that owns it is the real landmark. field_declaration and local_variable_declaration matched on a `declarator` field rather than a name: the identifier lives one level down in a variable_declarator, so the 'name' the generator found is the whole declarator. They are dropped as landmarks but kept as `variable` labels so a query summary still names them. import_declaration and package_declaration are the file preamble, never a place to bookmark inside; package_declaration keeps its `namespace` label (re-declared in add_labels, since dropping a landmark also drops its label) so a summary can still name the package. lambda_expression is added as a landmark: a Java lambda never wraps a declaration, so the generator cannot propose it no matter what the samples contain, but it is a real body worth bookmarking inside — a lambda passed to a stream or a Function field is exactly the code you want to return to. Like Python's lambda it has no name field, so it sticks while scrolling and the breadcrumb renderer skips it; it is deliberately not a container. annotation_type_declaration (`@interface Foo {}`) is added because it is a real top-level declaration the sample does not exercise — adding one purely to satisfy the generator would be sample padding, and it is labelled `interface`, which it structurally is. `constructor` is added as a container: the generator proposed it as a label but a constructor genuinely nests statements, and without it a bookmark inside a constructor shows the class but not the constructor it sits in. enum_constant stays as the generator proposed it, which is deliberate — a Java enum constant can carry a class body with overridden methods, so it really does contain declarations. record_declaration is kept and labelled `class`: it is a Java 16+ declaration the built-in Java profile does not know about at all, so this profile anchors records where the built-in silently cannot. The remaining add_labels carry no landmark or container weight and exist purely so a query summary reads in Java's own vocabulary: for_statement/while_statement/do_statement (the generator only observed enhanced_for_statement, the `for (T x : xs)` form), switch_block as `match` alongside the switch_expression the generator already labelled — note there is deliberately no `switch_statement` entry, because tree-sitter-java has no such kind: a `switch` in statement position parses as a switch_expression, and naming the kind that reads naturally is a lint error (`node kind 'switch_statement' is not defined by this grammar`) rather than a silent no-op — and try_statement/try_with_resources_statement/catch_clause/ternary_expression as `if statement` since the label set has no dedicated exception or ternary concept and these are the closest sanctioned fit.
